purpose: Plain-language descriptions of what each keybind actually does in-game, for the 238 keyboard-bound actions that have a display name but no real CIG-written description (see docs/finding-keybind-descriptions-closed.md - CIG only wrote 86 usable descriptions out of 1,103 actions, confirmed closed, do not re-chase). This is the drafting half of claude/plan-writing-keybind-descriptions.md - 'draft them from what we already know, then have Sleven correct rather than author.'
status: DRAFT. Every row is source: cc_draft - Sleven's own knowledge of the game, not this session's, is what makes these trustworthy. Do not present these to end users as verified until reviewed.
how_to_review: confidence:high = standard, unambiguous mechanic, low-risk to publish as-is - either self-evident from the label, or since the 2026-08-07 verification pass below, corroborated by an external fan reference that matches this draft closely. confidence:medium = plausible from the label/group/binding context, and for 9 rows now also corroborated at the category/mechanic level by an external fan reference (not CIG's own words) - worth a skim, not a rewrite. No rows remain at confidence:low as of the 2026-08-07 verification pass - the 5 that were now sit at medium or high; see verification_pass_2026-08-07b below for what changed and why.
join_key_warning: JOIN BY (action, map) TOGETHER, NEVER BY action ALONE. Confirmed this session: v_yaw_left/v_yaw_right mean 'yaw the ship's nose' under the spaceship_movement actionmap but 'turn the ground vehicle' under vehicle_driver - same action name, different meaning. A flat action-name lookup silently picks one and mislabels the other. This file carries both 'action' and 'map' on every row for exactly this reason; the join script that built it explicitly checks for this class of collision (0 others found, 238/238 rows joined, 0 missing) and the check is worth re-running any time this file is regenerated for a new patch.
specifically_flagged_for_a_look: RESOLVED by the 2026-08-07 verification pass, kept here for history: v_power_throttle_down/min/up/max (F9/F10) were flagged as possibly mislabeled - 'Decrease/Increase Throttle' grouped with power-triangle actions rather than flight throttle. An external fan keybind reference (scfocus.org, Alpha 4.8) independently places these same four actions inside its own 'Power Distribution' section, immediately after the weapons/engines/shields triangle controls and 'Reset Assignments' - not inside its separate flight-speed section. Confirms this is a reactor/power control, not ship speed. Exact step-size mechanic is still not confirmed in-game - kept at medium, not high.

RESOLVED by the 2026-08-07 verification pass, kept here for history: view_switch_to_alternative (Z) vs view_enable_camview_mode (F4) were both labeled identically ('Advanced Camera Controls Modifier (Hold)') with no clear distinction. scfocus.org's dedicated camera-controls page describes Z (HOLD) + mouse movement as orbiting the 3rd-person camera around a fixed focal point, while F4 is the separate modifier that unlocks the full offset/zoom/field-of-view/depth-of-field/preset adjustment set. Both descriptions rewritten to reflect this; confidence raised to medium (not high - still a fan source, not CIG's own words, and worth a glance in-game to confirm).
excluded_by_design: This file covers only the 238 actions that have BOTH a keyboard default AND a label AND no usable existing description - the same scope Sleven set in plan-writing-keybind-descriptions.md (a keyboard player can't press a joystick-only action, and an action with no display name never appears on CIG's own keybinding screen). It does NOT re-describe the 41 actions that already have a real, non-duplicate CIG description, and does not touch joystick/gamepad-only actions.
downstream: C1/Code: join this file to data-layer/processed/keybinds_site.json on (action, map) and wire desc/confidence into the page build (build_keybind_modes.py / kb_modes.gen.js) as the fallback description whenever keybinds_site.json's own 'desc' field is null or a duplicate of the label. Keep confidence and source alongside the text so the page can visually distinguish a CIG-written description from a cc_draft one, and so a future 'Sleven reviewed and approved' pass has something to flip.

The review pass called for in plan-writing-keybind-descriptions.md #6 (Sleven corrects rather than authors) still has not happened and these still ship as source: cc_draft, not source: cc / reviewed.
